messages:
mike: heads up — after the autoscaler changes we started seeing intermittent timeouts to model-store.vpce.redwood.internal from our us-west-2 GPU subnets. DNS resolves to VPC endpoint IPs but connections fail from some AZs. started ~09:10 UTC. anyone else?

lisa: ugh. can you paste dig +short for the name and which subnet/ip fails?

mike: sure — from a failing worker (subnet 10.10.42.0/24):
```
$ dig +short model-store.vpce.redwood.internal
10.10.11.45
10.10.23.78
10.10.42.93
```
then `curl -v https://model-store.vpce.redwood.internal/health` hangs then resets. from a healthy worker in a diff subnet (10.10.12.0/24) it works fine.

raj: quick checks: 1) make sure the VPC endpoint has Private DNS enabled 2) check endpoint SG inbound rules (endpoint SG must allow traffic from client SG or client CIDRs on 443) 3) check if there are multiple private hosted zones overlapping.

ellie: adding: when you see per-AZ differences it often maps to which ENI (interface endpoint) DNS returned. dig returned 3 IPs — one per AZ. If the SG attached to the ENI doesn't allow the source SG/CIDR for that AZ, it'll drop. Also check NACLs on the failing subnet — stateless NACL can break TCP handshakes.

mike: SG looks fine on paper — endpoint SG has a rule `Inbound: sg-client (sg-0abc123) TCP 443`. The clients in the failing subnet have that SG attached. NACLs are default allow. Weirdly the failing IP from dig above (10.10.42.93) maps to an ENI in the same AZ as the failing worker. ENI shows Attached, private-ip 10.10.42.93.

lisa: can you `traceroute -T -p 443 10.10.42.93` and tcpdump on the worker to see if SYN/ACK coming back?

mike: traceroute TCP shows SYN -> no reply. tcpdump shows SYN out, nothing back.

raj: two other causes we've hit: 1) endpoint SG references another SG that was recreated (rule now references an id that exists but is not the same security group owner) — SG rules matching by id are strict. 2) someone disabled the endpoint's security group egress to 0.0.0.0/0 (we lock egress on endpoint SG often). If endpoint SG egress is too restrictive the ENI can't talk back.

ellie: also check if anyone toggled source/dest check on the endpoint ENI (should be ON). If it was turned off by mistake and the ENI is part of some NAT/forwarding setup it can break pathing.

mike: checked: source/dest check is ON. endpoint SG egress only allows HTTPS to 10.10.0.0/16 (our VPC). Client SG is referenced correctly. No PHZ overlaps that I can find.

infra-bot: deploy: autoscaler-prod scaled +12 instances at 2026-03-05T09:07:18Z.

lisa: correlation looks strong — autoscaler created instances in AZ B, which shifted DNS round-robin weight; some ENIs may have been recreated with a different SG during the provisioning workflow. Can you `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=private-ip-address,Values=10.10.42.93` and paste associated SGs?

mike: output: ENI eni-0f1e2d3c, Groups: sg-0abc123 (endpoint-sg) and also sg-0deadbee (extra-sg). extra-sg looks like a leftover we added during a test last month. Its inbound rules are empty and it has no egress.

raj: bingo. If the ENI has multiple SGs and one of them has restrictive egress or no egress, AWS combines security group rules as a union for inbound and egress. BUT there is a quirk when a rule references a security group that was deleted and recreated with a different owner — the traffic can be blocked. More likely the extra-sg with no egress is not the problem by itself, but I bet the endpoint ENI's effective egress is limited by that extra-sg. For endpoints the ENI needs egress back to the client ephemeral ports.

ellie: quick experiment: temporarily remove the extra-sg from that ENI or add egress 1024-65535 to client CIDR and see if connection returns.

mike: removed extra-sg from ENI and curl started working immediately from the previously failing worker.

lisa: nice one. so root cause: ENI got associated with a stale/experimental SG that had restrictive egress during autoscale churn. That SG probably got attached via automation (packer/ami step or rollout script).

raj: follow-ups: 1) add a linting check in infra-as-code to prevent attaching extra-sg to interface endpoints 2) update runbook to check ENI SG list when a VPCE is flaky 3) consider making endpoint SG rules reference client SGs (not CIDRs) to avoid accidental egress holes.

mike: I'll clean up the stale SG and add a preventative check to the ASG lifecycle hook. thanks all :thumbsup:

ellie: leaving a short note for oncall runbook: `private-link: if some AZs fail but DNS resolves -> check endpoint ENI SGs (no leftover restrictive SGs), check egress rules allow ephemeral ports back to client, ensure Private DNS enabled, verify NACLs`

mike: tagging @infra-sre FYI — will roll a small patch to ASG lifecycle tonight to avoid attaching the test-sg.

infra-bot: note: incident-created? no — resolved by config change at 2026-03-05T09:22:01Z.
